jobs.title: RUST_CODE.BBS · The banner
jobs.prompt: a four-panel newspaper comic strip, four equal panels in a single horizontal row with thin black gutters (4 panels). Style: comic strip panel, black brush-pen ink line with muddy early-2000s digital flat colors, rubbery kinetic linework, mid-2000s webcomic look, limited palette, slightly misregistered fills. Cast, the same faces, hair and builds in every panel, ages exactly as given: WOOD — aged 26, thin man, hunched, unshaven, tired bloodshot eyes, ink on his right knuckle; BARNABY (the dog) — a low-slung terrier and hound mix, long body, short legs, folded velvet ears, wiry white-and-tan coat, gray on the muzzle from 2004, cloudy eyes from 2009, carried from 2010. WOOD usually wears black hoodie open over a faded band tee; the brown chore coat outdoors; dark jeans. Clothes, hair-dos and anything held come from this strip's description, never from the reference sheet; hands are empty unless a panel names what they hold. Title of the strip: BACKUP. The strip: The garage's monitor one night shows a board Wood didn't dial: a banner in phosphor green — WELCOME TO a name, a frontier, ACTIVE NODES: 64 — and the stick chorus on the desk reading it with him. The strip draws the banner as shapes. The chorus can read it. Wood can't. Panel 1: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, a thin man at a beige computer whose screen shows a banner of green blocks across the top, tiny stick figures on the desk (in this panel: WOOD, BARNABY (the dog)). No dialogue in this panel. Panel 2: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, close on a computer screen with three lines of phosphor-green blocks and a two-digit number drawn as shapes at the end. No dialogue in this panel. Panel 3: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, tiny stick figures on a desk pointing at a screen with tiny empty speech balloons. No dialogue in this panel. Panel 4: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, a thin man at a computer speaking down to tiny stick figures on his desk (in this panel: WOOD). Wood says "I didn't dial that.". Lettering: every balloon and caption contains its complete text exactly as written, in clean hand-lettered comic capitals, large enough to read; size each balloon to fit its whole sentence and never cut a word at a balloon or panel edge; no words other than the ones given. Bottom right margin: tiny signature "A. Finch — Small Wood, OR" beside a tiny stylized gull, two strokes. Reference @barnaby is the model sheet for BARNABY (the dog): match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @chorus_and_meme is a finished strip in this style. Reference @wood_26 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Match the attached references: @barnaby for the character Barnaby; @chorus_and_meme for the character; @wood_26 for the character Wood at 24-31.
